heading: Nuclear Energy Intelligence
subheading: Small modular reactors, uranium & the AI power-demand trade
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. SMR developers are pre-revenue with long regulatory timelines; verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Oklo closed Oct 23 at $26.35 (52-week range $26.07-$152.06; ~$4.9B market cap), down ~15% in the week to Oct 19 after a hot September CPI sent the 10-year yield to 5.26% on Oct 14 — Piper, Barclays, Citi and Truist have all cut targets (Truist to $31, Citi to $33) and analysts see ~$6.5B of cash burn before 2030 against $3.0B in cash at June 30, with a ~$1B ATM live

The TradeTech long-term indicator is $97/lb (contract price $96.50 at end-September) and spot has held about $89.6-90, yet Cameco is ~42% below its high, URA is -27% over a year and SPUT traded ~11.6% below NAV on Oct 9 — physical uranium is firm while listed nuclear equities keep de-rating

kpis.sub: X-ENERGY / AMAZON / AEP INDIANA XE-100 PLAN
kpis.label: Announced Oct 19: a joint development agreement for a proposed 12-unit Xe-100 plant at the former Breed coal site in Sullivan County, Indiana, with Amazon funding development and a long-term PPA — but it is evaluation-stage only (no final investment decision, no construction dates) and sits beside Amazon's 690 MW Calvert Cliffs deal with Constellation (Oct 1)

The NRC's Sep 29 Clinch River BWRX-300 construction permit and TerraPower's Natrium construction (under way since April 2026) are real milestones, but no commercial SMR is operating — and Barclays' Oct 20 NuScale downgrade cited commercial delays and contract uncertainty

private_watchlist.name: TerraPower

No new dated item this week.

bear_case.title: The whole SMR group keeps making new lows
bear_case.description: Oklo ($26.35), NuScale ($5.38), Centrus ($102.45) and X-energy ($10.60) all sit at or near 52-week lows as of Oct 23, a second straight week of losses despite a licence milestone (Clinch River), the Amazon/AEP Indiana plan and record long-term uranium prices. Rates (10-year at 5.26%) and dilution, not headlines, are setting prices. Counter: drawdowns of this size reset entry prices, and analysts argue the selling is rate-driven rather than a business deterioration.

bear_case.title: Dilution is the real funding model
bear_case.description: Oklo's ~$1B ATM (about a fifth of the company), NuScale's $750M ATM and Centrus's $500M offering mean each upbeat announcement can be financed by selling stock into it; Oklo alone is projected to burn ~$6.5B before 2030 against $3.0B in cash. Counter: raising capital is how pre-revenue builders fund long-lead projects.

bear_case.title: Analysts are capitulating on targets
bear_case.description: Barclays moved NuScale to Underweight and Citi to Sell ($4); Oklo targets were cut by Piper, Barclays, Citi and Truist in one week; Centrus targets were cut by UBS, Roth, Barclays and Truist. Counter: sell-side cuts often arrive near lows, and consensus remains Buy on most names.

bear_case.title: A permit or a development agreement is not an operating reactor
bear_case.description: The NRC's Clinch River permit authorizes construction only, X-energy's 960 MW Indiana plan has no final investment decision, NuScale has no binding order, and there are still zero commercial SMRs operating. Counter: TerraPower is already building Natrium and TVA is moving ahead of schedule.

bear_case.title: Physical uranium is strong but equities are not following
bear_case.description: Long-term uranium at $97/lb is near a 19-year high, yet Cameco is ~42% below its high, URA is down ~27% over a year and SPUT trades at an ~11-13% discount to NAV; Westinghouse's IPO value remains contested. Counter: a widening gap can also close from the equity side.

bear_case.title: Hyperscaler money is going to old reactors, not new designs
bear_case.description: Google's 890 MW and Amazon's 690 MW deals sit on Constellation's existing fleet and uprates, with new capacity only in the 2028-2032 window — favouring operators over pre-revenue SMR developers, while gas and renewables remain faster to build.
